caption:
Equifax Settlement Per Person: Up to $2.89 of Fund

Equifax settlement per person, in one number. About 147 million people affected by the 2017 data breach. Up to $425 million in the FTC settlement fund. That is up to $2.89 of fund per person (our math), and it was a fund for claims, not a check.

Sources: Equifax 8-K Ex. 99.1 (Sep 7, 2017); FTC press release (Jul 22, 2019).

descripcion:
Equifax settlement per person: how much was the 2017 data breach settlement really worth? About 147 million people were affected. The FTC settlement made available up to $425 million for them. Split across everyone, that is up to $2.89 of fund per person (our math).

What happened: in September 2017 Equifax disclosed a breach of personal data. Its press release that week, filed with the SEC as an exhibit to an 8-K (the form a public company uses to report major events), quoted the CEO: "We pride ourselves on being a leader in managing and protecting data." In July 2019 the FTC announced a settlement that made available up to $425 million to help people affected by the breach.

Did everyone get a check? No. It was a fund people had to claim from, not a payment sent to each person. That is why "how much will I get" never had a simple answer.

This video is about the 2017 data breach settlement announced in 2019, not any newer Equifax case.

Sources: Equifax 8-K, Exhibit 99.1, Sep 7, 2017; FTC press release, Jul 22, 2019.

narracion: One hundred forty-seven MILLION people. One breach. And that same week? Equifax's CEO said... this. Two years later, the F.T.C. settlement? Up to four hundred twenty-five million dollars. Sounds huge, right? Now split it across about a hundred forty-seven million people... Up to two dollars eighty-nine of fund per person. Not even a coffee. And it's a fund for claims, not a check. Wild.
